shots.phrase: Begin by framing Pipeline Foundation as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
The OpenGL graphics pipeline processes vertices through programmable shader stages.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Primitive Assembly precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Three connected vertices form a triangle primitive, which the pipeline then processes as a single geometric unit for rendering.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how Clipping Stage operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: A triangle extending beyond the camera's frustum is sliced at the clipping plane boundaries, discarding the exterior segments.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Rasterization and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: Each triangle is subdivided into pixel-aligned fragments, with each fragment receiving interpolated attributes for downstream processing.
Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
Apply Interpolation to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Interpolation produces per-fragment values from vertex outputs.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Fragment Processing, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Fragment shaders evaluate lighting equations and material properties to generate final color and alpha values for each pixel.
Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
Stress-test the reasoning around Depth Testing with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Depth testing resolves visibility according to stored depth values.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Blending to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Blending combines a fragment result with an existing framebuffer value.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Coordinate Spaces to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Coordinate spaces, sampling, and numerical precision must remain explicit.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Visual correctness follows from explicit conventions, assumptions, sampling decisions, and measurable error.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
